_meta.model: Recentered AI-effectiveness threshold: what clinical AI must do to offset the mortality attributable to primary-care erosion, without widening inequality.
_meta.target: primary-care-supply-attributable excess mortality (NOT the poverty-driven SVI mortality gap)
_meta.note_on_gradient: Basu 2019 found the primary-care decline was NOT disproportionate by county poverty or race; it was concentrated in rural areas. We therefore apply the decline uniformly by vulnerability (loss proportional to baseline mortality) and locate inequality in the REACH gradient (lower AI uptake in high-vulnerability communities). Rural vs urban decline is reported as a sensitivity.

mortality.source: CDC WONDER age-adjusted all-cause mortality by CDC Social Vulnerability Index quartile
mortality.note: Age-adjusted all-cause mortality by SVI quartile; used as annual deaths per 1,000 residents

pcp_supply.source: Basu 2019 JAMA Intern Med: PCP density fell 46.6 to 41.4 per 100,000 nationally, 2005-2015 (within-county mean -5.2; -4.2 to -4.4 at primary-care-service-area and hospital-referral-region levels)

mortality_elasticity.source: Basu 2019 JAMA Intern Med: per 10 additional PCP/100k, cause-specific mortality reductions of 0.9% (cardiovascular), 1.0% (cancer), 1.4% (respiratory); cause shares from CDC leading causes of death
mortality_elasticity.elasticity_range_note: Assumed range around the derived point estimate (0.59%); not reported as a range in the source

ai_reach.source: assumption anchored to digital-health uptake gradients (Rodriguez 2020 JAMA), which are lower in high-vulnerability communities

adequacy_sensitivity.source: HRSA/NCHWA Physician Workforce: Projections 2023-2038 (Dec 2025) projects a shortage of 70,610 primary care physicians by 2038 (~20 per 100,000 over the US population; point estimate); AAMC 2024 projects 20,200-40,400 primary care physicians by 2036 and Bazemore 2024 estimates growth needs through 2040 (used to bound the sensitivity range)
adequacy_sensitivity.range_note: Range spans published projections: lower bound 6 per 100,000 = AAMC 2024 low projection (20,200 primary care physicians by 2036) over ~340 million US residents; point and upper bound 20.3 = HRSA/NCHWA shortage of 70,610 by 2038, the highest published projection. A shortage relative to projected demand, treated as a supply deficit of equal size.

capacity_discount.source: Formalizes the elasticity-symmetry assumption (physician-equivalent capacity added through efficiency has the same mortality value as capacity added through hiring) as an explicit, varied parameter rather than a fixed, unstated assumption. Point estimate 1.0 reproduces the base-case symmetric assumption; the range extends to 0.5 (a throughput-increased visit delivers half the mortality-relevant value of an additional physician) as an unvalidated bounding scenario, since no study has directly compared the two margins on a mortality outcome.

benchmarks.source: Disease-specific AI effect transmitted to all-cause mortality in code (base: CV-death pathway; sensitivity: trial all-cause pathway).

ai_htn.sbp_source: Ong 2026 EClinicalMedicine meta-analysis of RCTs: AI-based mobile health interventions, SBP mean difference -3.18 mmHg (95% CI -5.50 to -0.86); low certainty
ai_htn.allcause_source: Ettehad 2016 Lancet meta-analysis of 123 BP-lowering RCTs: all-cause mortality RR 0.87 (0.84-0.91) per 10 mmHg SBP reduction
ai_htn.mace_source: BPLTTC 2021 Lancet IPD: major cardiovascular events HR ~0.90 per 5 mmHg (cardiovascular-event transmission; reported as a sensitivity only, not an all-cause effect)
ai_htn.cvdeath_source: BPLTTC 2021 Lancet IPD (48 RCTs): 5 mm Hg SBP reduction reduced cardiovascular death by 5%; all-cause transmission = 1 - cv_share*(1 - HR_cvdeath^(SBP/5)), non-cardiovascular deaths assigned no effect (parallel to the cause-specific construction of the benchmark)

digital_htn_proxy.sbp_source: Lindsay-Perez 2025 J Hum Hypertens: digital (non-AI) lifestyle interventions in hypertension; comparison only

ai_mortality_upper_bound.source: Lin 2024 Nat Med pragmatic RCT: AI-ECG alert, 90-day all-cause mortality among hospitalized patients (not primary care); upper-bound scenario only

distributions.elasticity: uniform over published range (no distributional information)
distributions.supply_loss_realized: uniform 4.2-5.2 (range across geographic units in source)
distributions.supply_loss_projected: triangular(6, 20.3, 20.3): mode at the HRSA point, which is also the highest published projection
